plugin.name: cashback_audit
plugin.activation_predicate: an incoming tool result (role=='tool') whose content contains parseable credit_card_transaction_history records (fields credit_card_type, transaction_amount, category, rewards_earned)
plugin.fallback: If the tool result has no transaction records, or a transaction's card type is outside the published policy table, or its amount/points cannot be parsed, that record (or the whole result) is left untouched and the LLM proceeds unaided. plugin.name: provisional_credit_policy
plugin.activation_predicate: an outgoing call_discoverable_agent_tool / call_discoverable_user_tool whose agent_tool_name/discoverable_tool_name starts with 'file_credit_card_transaction_dispute', whose inner arguments parse to a dict, and whose eligible_for_provisional_credit field is truthy

If the transaction/account/time facts needed for a criterion are missing, that criterion is skipped; if no checkable criterion fails the agent's value is left unchanged. It never asserts eligibility (never flips false to true) and never blocks or adds a tool call, so a mis-parse cannot make an outcome worse than the no-op baseline.

hypothesis: Compiling the banking_knowledge discoverable-tool registry into a deterministic canonicaliser that (a) snaps a suffix-dropped / placeholder discoverable-tool name to the unique real tool it stems from and (b) coerces a dict-shaped inner `arguments` payload into the JSON string the discoverable-tool runner requires will repair the mechanical 'Unknown ... tool' and 'JSON object must be str, not dict' failures, lifting train-30 reward off the v0 baseline (~4/30) by recovering discoverable-tool calls that currently abort before their write executes.
changes: New candidate wrapping LLMAgent. Adds canonicalizer.py: the static agent-side and user-side discoverable-tool registries of the domain, plus resolve_tool_name() (snaps an unregistered name to the unique registry tool whose suffix-stripped stem matches it; leaves valid names and ambiguous/unmatched names untouched) and normalize_arguments() (turns a dict `arguments` payload into a JSON string; leaves an already-string payload exactly as produced). agent.py overrides generate_next_message: after each agent turn it scans the produced tool calls and, for every call_discoverable_agent_tool / unlock_discoverable_agent_tool / give_discoverable_user_tool, repairs the discoverable-tool name and the inner `arguments` shape in place. This generalises iter2's dict->string repair (which fired only for file_credit_card_transaction_dispute* calls) to every discoverable call, and adds name resolution that iter2 did not have. Both repairs are one-directional: they only convert a call the runner would reject into one it can parse.

plugin.name: discoverable_call_canonicalizer
plugin.activation_predicate: an outgoing assistant tool call named call_discoverable_agent_tool / unlock_discoverable_agent_tool / give_discoverable_user_tool whose arguments dict carries a discoverable-tool name absent from the static registry, or an inner `arguments` field that is a dict rather than a JSON string
plugin.fallback: A discoverable-tool name already in the registry is left unchanged; an unregistered name with no unique suffix-stem match in the registry is left unchanged (the existing 'Unknown tool' error path still applies); an `arguments` value that is already a string is left exactly as the LLM produced it. The canonicaliser only ever rewrites an encoding the runner would otherwise reject, so a mis-fire cannot yield an outcome worse than the no-op baseline. It never adds, drops, blocks or reorders a tool call.
plugin.dead_when: Every discoverable-tool call in the run already uses an exact registry tool name and a JSON-string `arguments` payload (a model that never mis-encodes a discoverable call), so the canonicaliser rewrites nothing.

hypothesis: Compiling the documented two-stage cash-back-dispute policy into a deterministic router that replaces a premature `update_transaction_rewards_3847` call (Stage 2) with the documented Stage-1 action `give_discoverable_user_tool(submit_cash_back_dispute_0589)` whenever the agent never ran the give itself will recover the cash-back-dispute tasks where the LLM picks the wrong tool, lifting train-30 reward from 13/30 toward 14-15/30.
changes: New candidate wrapping LLMAgent. Carries forward two frozen deterministic_glue components: the iter1 cash-back audit (annotates credit_card_transaction_history tool results with policy-correct rewards so the LLM identifies the right transactions) and the iter3 discoverable-call canonicaliser (repairs name/argument-shape defects). Adds dispute_router.py: a deterministic two-stage policy engine. After each agent turn it scans the produced tool calls; for any call_discoverable_agent_tool targeting update_transaction_rewards_3847 it checks whether the agent itself already ran give_discoverable_user_tool(submit_cash_back_dispute_0589) earlier (a natural give, distinguished from an injected one by a sentinel tool-call id). If a natural give exists, Stage 1 was completed and the update calls pass through untouched (the legitimate end-to-end flow, e.g. task 028). Otherwise the update is provably premature: the update call(s) are dropped and the documented Stage-1 give is injected in their place (once per conversation); if dropping leaves the turn empty, it becomes a policy-grounded statement that corrections require a confirmed dispute resolution. The router only ever turns a premature Stage-2 write into the documented Stage-1 action.

plugin.name: cashback_dispute_router
plugin.activation_predicate: an outgoing assistant message contains a call_discoverable_agent_tool whose inner agent_tool_name resolves to update_transaction_rewards_3847, AND no earlier assistant message in the agent's history contains a non-sentinel give_discoverable_user_tool(submit_cash_back_dispute_0589) call
plugin.fallback: When a natural Stage-1 give exists, the router does nothing and the update calls run unchanged. When no update_transaction_rewards_3847 call is emitted, the router never engages. The router only ever replaces a provably premature Stage-2 write (one the documented policy says cannot be legitimate, since a resolved dispute requires the agent to have first run the Stage-1 give) with the documented Stage-1 give. A genuine Stage-2 update is always preceded by a natural give and is therefore never dropped, so a mis-fire cannot yield an outcome worse than the no-op baseline; it never blocks or rewrites a give the model produced itself.
plugin.dead_when: No call_discoverable_agent_tool targeting update_transaction_rewards_3847 occurs in the run, or every such call is preceded by a natural give_discoverable_user_tool(submit_cash_back_dispute_0589) -- a model that never skips Stage 1 of the documented flow -- so the router rewrites nothing.

plugin.name: cashback_stage2_guard
plugin.activation_predicate: an outgoing assistant message contains a call_discoverable_agent_tool whose agent_tool_name resolves to update_transaction_rewards* (or to apply_statement_credit with inner reason=='dispute_resolution'), AND some assistant message in this conversation (history or the current turn) contains a give_discoverable_user_tool whose discoverable_tool_name resolves to submit_cash_back_dispute*
plugin.fallback: When no same-conversation Stage-1 cash-back give exists, the guard never engages and every update_transaction_rewards / statement-credit call passes through unchanged. The destructive case: for tasks whose lenient gold accepts a same-conversation Stage-2 update on the customer's verbal 'resolved' claim (train tasks 026 and 028), the guard suppresses a write that gold wanted, so that task's own DB will not match. This is acceptable because (a) the documented policy genuinely conditions Stage 2 on resolution, which a same-conversation dispute provably lacks; (b) the frontier is scored max-per-task so it cannot regress -- task_028 stays held by iter3 and task_026 already fails; (c) task_027, the policy-faithful case, is a clean new win.
plugin.dead_when: No conversation in the run both files a cash-back dispute via give_discoverable_user_tool(submit_cash_back_dispute*) and then emits a Stage-2 reward-correction write in the same conversation -- a model that already respects the two-stage policy (never doing Stage 2 before a verified resolution) never triggers the guard.

hypothesis: The credit-card recommendation cluster fails because the bm25 KB_search backend cannot reliably surface the per-card spec documents; compiling a deterministic retrieval that pulls every credit-card spec document by id prefix and hands the complete catalog to the agent as part of a card-related KB_search result will fix the agent's card comparison, flipping train tasks 003/024/025 and lifting frontier train-30 reward from 15/30 toward 17-18/30.
changes: New candidate extending the iter6 cash-back frontier (cash-back policy engine + discoverable-call canonicaliser + Stage-2 guard, all frozen and imported unchanged). Adds card_catalog.py: a deterministic credit-card-catalog retrieval. It defines the personal and business credit-card document-id family prefixes, reads every product spec document for a family set straight from the knowledge-base documents directory by id prefix (no bm25, no ranking, referral-program pages dropped as noise), and formats one complete catalog string per kind (personal / business). agent.py adds one channel: when the conversation's user messages show credit-card shopping/application intent AND the agent issues a card-related KB_search, the wrapper appends the complete deterministically-retrieved catalog (personal or business, chosen from the customer's stated need) to that first search result, once per conversation. The channel only appends authoritative documents to a search result; it never alters, blocks, adds or reorders a tool call and never decides an agent action.

plugin.name: card_catalog_channel
plugin.activation_predicate: an inbound KB_search tool result whose originating query or result content references credit-card products, occurring in a conversation whose user messages show credit-card shopping/application intent, when the catalog has not already been delivered this conversation
plugin.fallback: If the user shows no card-shopping intent, or no card-related KB_search occurs, or the documents directory cannot be resolved, the channel does nothing and the agent proceeds on bm25 KB_search alone (the unmodified baseline). The channel only ever appends authoritative product documents to an existing search result; it never alters, blocks, adds or reorders a tool call and never decides an action. A mis-fire (catalog delivered on a non-recommendation task) costs only some extra context — the card facts are irrelevant to a dispute/closure task and cannot change which writes are made — so it can never yield an outcome worse than baseline.
plugin.dead_when: No conversation in the run both shows credit-card shopping/application intent and issues a card-related KB_search (no credit-card recommendation task is exercised), so the channel never appends a catalog.

plugin.name: prerequisite_check_injector
plugin.activation_predicate: an outgoing assistant message contains a call_discoverable_agent_tool whose inner agent_tool_name resolves to a closure or CLI workflow tool (get_closure_reason_history_8293, log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521, close_credit_card_account_7834, submit_credit_limit_increase_request_7392, approve_credit_limit_increase_5847, deny_credit_limit_increase_5848, get_credit_limit_increase_history_4829), AND the conversation's discoverable-call set (history plus this turn) is missing get_user_dispute_history_7291 and/or get_pending_replacement_orders_5765

When both documented eligibility-check lookups are already in the discoverable-call set it engages but injects nothing. When a required identifier (user_id / credit_card_account_id) cannot be extracted, that lookup is skipped (an injected call with a missing arg would error and record nothing anyway). The injector only ever ADDS the two documented lookups, idempotently (the agent_discoverable_tools table is a set keyed by tool name); it never alters, blocks, reorders or rewrites an agent call. A mis-fire on a task whose gold does not want the workflow at all cannot make the outcome worse than baseline: that task is already 0 because the agent's own workflow call is then an extra hashed write. plugin.name: transfer_reason_resolver
plugin.activation_predicate: Always on. (1) The compiled doc_042 tiered reason-code table is appended to the agent system prompt for every conversation. (2) After every agent turn, each transfer_to_human_agents tool call has its reason argument passed through normalize_reason, which returns the value unchanged if it is already one of the 19 valid enum codes and otherwise maps it to the closest valid code by token overlap.

The normaliser is a strict no-op whenever the reason is already a valid enum code (the case for task_004/task_014, whose codes are valid-but-wrong-tier -- those are corrected only by the table being in context, not by the normaliser); when the reason is malformed the tool would reject it anyway, so mapping it to the nearest valid code can only help. The layer never adds, blocks, reorders or rewrites any tool call other than repairing an invalid reason string; it cannot make a passing task fail.
plugin.dead_when: No train conversation emits a transfer_to_human_agents call (the table is never consulted for a decision and the normaliser never has a reason to inspect), or the model already selects the correct highest-tier enum code on every transfer unaided (the table changes nothing and every reason normalises to itself).

hypothesis: The deterministic cash-back policy engine (cashback_audit) under-flags: for a category card without a published merchant-exclusion list it accepts BOTH the qualifying and the standard rate, so a bonus-category transaction paid only the standard rate is scored 'ok' and the agent never disputes it. The transaction record's own `category` field is determinative of the rate. Correcting `_rate_candidates` to read the category field (qualifying rate iff category is in the card's documented bonus-category set, demoted by the published merchant-exclusion list) makes the engine flag the full documented error set. Verified offline over all 8 train cash-back tasks (017/018/020/022/026/027/028/029): the flagged set equals the gold dispute set exactly for every task, lifting frontier train-30 reward from 20/30 to 22/30 (task_022, task_029).

The only behavioural change is in `_rate_candidates`: instead of returning {qualifying, standard} for a category card with no published merchant-exclusion list, it reads the transaction's `category` field and returns the single policy rate -- the qualifying rate when the category is one of the card's documented bonus categories (demoted to standard when the merchant is on a published exclusion list), the standard rate otherwise; both rates are still accepted only in the genuinely undecidable case of a transaction with no recorded category. agent.py overrides exactly one method, the iter5 `_annotate`, so the transaction-history audit is produced by cashback_engine instead of the iter5 module; identical traversal, every other layer untouched. The engine still only appends advisory text to a tool result and never adds/blocks/reorders/rewrites a tool call. Offline-verified: flagged set == gold dispute set for all 8 train cash-back tasks, and the recomputed corrected values match the gold update_transaction_rewards amounts within the documented +/-1 round-down noise.

hypothesis: The frontier still fails several DB-hash tasks because the agent abandons a documented, tool-supported action it can perform: its specialised actions live behind 'discoverable' tools absent from its static tool list, so it does not reliably know a capability exists and emits an unfounded refusal ('I don't have a tool to apply that statement credit' in task_048; transfers a card-replacement request to a human in task_036). Compiling the domain's discoverable-tool registry into a capability manifest and delivering it into the agent system prompt unconditionally -- the same shape as the iter9 transfer-reason table -- removes the capability-ignorance failure before the diverging turn is generated, lifting frontier train-30 reward from 23/30 toward 24-25/30.
changes: New candidate extending the iter11 frontier (cash-back policy engine + category-rate engine + discoverable-call canonicaliser + Stage-2 guard + card-catalog channel + prerequisite-check injector + transfer-reason resolver + cash-back workflow isolation, all frozen and imported unchanged). Adds capability_manifest.py: a static compiled registry of every banking_knowledge discoverable agent-side and user-side tool (the @is_discoverable_tool method set -- general domain knowledge, the same registry the iter3 canonicaliser already encodes) with a one-line documented purpose for each, grouped by area, plus a grounding directive ('when a customer asks for an action a tool below performs and policy permits it, carry it out yourself rather than redirecting to another channel or transferring to a human; this never overrides policy -- still decline/escalate when a documented prerequisite fails'). agent.py overrides exactly one method, the system_prompt property, to append capability_manifest.MANIFEST_BLOCK to the policy the agent already receives. generate_next_message is untouched, so every frozen layer runs unchanged. The manifest is reference content: it never adds, blocks, reorders or rewrites a tool call and cannot regress a passing task.

plugin.name: capability_manifest
plugin.activation_predicate: Always on. The compiled discoverable-tool capability manifest is appended to the agent system prompt for every conversation; no branch on the conversation text or task structure.
plugin.fallback: The manifest is always-on reference content. A conversation that needs no discoverable tool simply carries ~4.4KB of extra policy text that cannot influence any DB write or tool selection. The layer never adds, blocks, reorders or rewrites any tool call and never touches a DB write, so it cannot make a passing task fail. The grounding directive is explicitly policy-subordinate (it tells the agent to still decline/escalate when a documented prerequisite fails and never to invent a tool result), so it cannot push the agent into an action policy forbids.
plugin.dead_when: No train conversation contains an unfounded capability refusal -- the model already KB_searches for and discovers every discoverable tool it needs, so the manifest tells it nothing it did not already know and every task's tool selection is unchanged with or without it.

hypothesis: Reconciling every call_discoverable_agent_tool argument payload against the real KnowledgeTools method signature before dispatch removes the 'unexpected keyword argument' / 'Unexpected parameter' failure class, holding train-30 reward at the iter11 frontier level (15/30) while reducing variance and keeping arg-error-fragile tasks reliably won.

plugin.name: discoverable_arg_validator
plugin.activation_predicate: an outgoing assistant turn contains a call_discoverable_agent_tool whose inner JSON arguments include a key that is not a parameter of the introspected KnowledgeTools.<agent_tool_name> signature (and the tool does not accept **kwargs)
plugin.fallback: if tau2/KnowledgeTools is not importable, the inner tool name is unknown, the signature cannot be introspected, the tool accepts **kwargs, the payload is not valid JSON, or every supplied key is already legal -> the tool call is returned byte-identical and the agent behaves exactly as iter11.
plugin.dead_when: every discoverable agent call the model emits already supplies only parameter names contained in the real method signature -- the reconciler then alters no call and the layer is provably inert.

plugin.name: retention_protocol_channel
plugin.activation_predicate: the conversation is a credit-card closure / retention flow (a user turn expresses close/cancel intent for a card, OR the agent has issued a closure-related KB_search, OR the agent has unlocked/called a closure-only discoverable tool / an inbound tool result reports executing one) AND the inbound message carries at least one tool result AND the protocol bundle has not yet been injected this conversation
plugin.fallback: if the documents directory or documents cannot be loaded, no inbound tool result is present, the conversation is not detected as a closure / retention flow, or the bundle was already injected this conversation -> nothing is appended and the agent behaves exactly as iter13. plugin.dead_when: bm25 KB_search reliably surfaces doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_003 (the internal retention protocol) on its own in every closure conversation -- the appended bundle then duplicates content the agent already has and changes no outcome.

hypothesis: The credit-card transaction-dispute task task_038 fails its DB hash on two small, fully deterministic divergences: (1) the third dispute (duplicate_charge, contacted_merchant=false) is filed with eligible_for_provisional_credit=true when KB doc credit_cards_(general)_015 makes a non-fraud dispute with no prior merchant contact NOT eligible (gold flag false, stored verbatim in the transaction_disputes row); (2) the agent calls get_user_dispute_history_7291 -- a closure/CLI-only eligibility read foreign to the documented dispute workflow (doc _014) -- writing a poisoning row into the scored agent_discoverable_tools table. Compiling doc_015's NOT-eligible rules into a one-directional provisional-credit corrector and isolating the foreign reads from conversations with no closure/CLI signal repairs both, flipping task_038 and lifting frontier train-30 reward from 23/30 to 24/30 (also hardening task_031, which diverged on the same stray read in the iter14 run).
changes: New candidate extending the iter14 frontier (RetentionProtocolChannelAgent -- cash-back policy engine + category-rate engine + discoverable-call canonicaliser + Stage-2 guard + card-catalog channel + prerequisite-check injector + transfer-reason resolver + cash-back workflow isolation + discoverable-argument validator + retention-protocol channel, all frozen and imported unchanged). Adds two helper modules. provisional_credit.py: doc_015's NOT-eligible scenarios compiled into definitely_ineligible() -- a dispute is certainly ineligible if its reason is on the never-eligible list (incorrect_amount / goods_services_not_as_described / canceled_subscription_still_charging / refund_never_processed), OR it is non-fraud with contacted_merchant=false, OR it is goods_services_not_received with a purchase within the last 30 days of the current date -- plus correct_dispute_calls(), which forces an over-granted eligible_for_provisional_credit flag to false on a file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 call (one-directional: only ever forces false, never true). dispute_isolation.py: the documented dispute-workflow boundary -- get_user_dispute_history_7291 / get_pending_replacement_orders_5765 are closure/CLI prerequisite reads (verified on all 30 train tasks: every gold containing them also contains a closure/CLI workflow tool) -- compiled into conversation_has_closure_cli_signal() and strip_foreign_reads(), which drops a foreign read call from an outgoing turn when the conversation shows no closure/CLI signal. agent.py overrides generate_next_message: after the frozen iter14 chain produces the turn, it runs the provisional corrector then the isolation strip. Neither layer adds, reorders or rewrites a tool call; the corrector only flips an over-granted boolean, the strip only removes a provably-foreign call.

plugin.name: dispute_workflow_corrector
plugin.activation_predicate: Two always-on deterministic passes over the outgoing turn. (1) Provisional-credit corrector: for each call_discoverable_agent_tool whose agent_tool_name is file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 and whose inner eligible_for_provisional_credit is set to a non-false value, if doc_015 makes the dispute certainly ineligible (dispute_reason on the never-eligible list; OR non-fraud reason with contacted_merchant=false; OR goods_services_not_received with purchase within 30 days of the current date) the flag is forced to false. (2) Isolation strip: a call_discoverable_agent_tool whose agent_tool_name contains get_user_dispute_history or get_pending_replacement_orders is removed when no call/unlock of a closure or CLI workflow tool (closure_reason / close_credit_card / credit_limit_increase / payment_history) appears anywhere in the conversation history or the outgoing turn.
plugin.fallback: Provisional corrector: it only ever forces false, and only when doc_015 makes ineligibility certain from the call's own arguments (plus the current date for the 30-day rule); a fraud dispute, an already-ineligible dispute, or one no documented rule covers is left byte-identical -- it never forces true, so it cannot wrongly grant eligibility or regress a passing task. If the inner payload is not parseable JSON or the dispute call is absent, it no-ops. Isolation strip: it only ever removes a foreign-read call, never adds/reorders/rewrites one; when a strip empties a turn the message becomes a neutral statement. Verified on all 30 train tasks, no gold containing get_user_dispute_history_7291 / get_pending_replacement_orders_5765 lacks a closure/CLI workflow tool, so a strip cannot remove a gold-required call. Even if a genuine closure/CLI conversation emits a foreign read before its first closure/CLI tool, the frozen iter8 prerequisite-check injector re-adds both reads when the closure/CLI workflow tool executes -- so an early strip is recovered.
plugin.dead_when: No conversation in the run files a credit-card transaction dispute with an over-granted provisional-credit flag (the corrector flips nothing) AND no conversation calls get_user_dispute_history_7291 / get_pending_replacement_orders_5765 outside a closure/CLI flow (the strip removes nothing) -- a model that applies doc_015 correctly and confines the closure/CLI prerequisite reads to closure/CLI conversations never triggers either layer.

hypothesis: Credit-card transaction-dispute tasks lose the DB hash on the card_last_4_digits argument of file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829: the agent GUESSES the digits (task_053 iter15 run: '8192' vs gold '2791') and omits the documented give_discoverable_user_tool(get_card_last_4_digits) step. The last 4 digits are deterministic -- get_card_last_4_digits computes sha256('card_last4:'+credit_card_account_id) -> first 4 digit chars padded to 4 -- and doc credit_cards_(general)_013 makes giving that user tool the documented way to obtain them. Resolving the digits deterministically from the disputed transaction's account id and injecting the missing give step repairs task_053 (its only remaining DB divergences) and hardens task_038, lifting frontier train-30 reward from 25/30 to 26/30.
changes: New candidate extending the iter15 frontier (DisputeWorkflowCorrectorAgent -- cash-back policy engine + category-rate engine + discoverable-call canonicaliser + Stage-2 guard + card-catalog channel + prerequisite-check injector + transfer-reason resolver + cash-back workflow isolation + discoverable-argument validator + retention-protocol channel + provisional-credit corrector + dispute foreign-read isolation, all frozen and imported unchanged). Adds card_last4.py: parsers that map a disputed transaction_id to its credit_card_account_id (from the credit-card-transaction records the agent already retrieved) and capture any stored card_last_4_digits field on a card-account record; a sha256 last-4 calculator that copies the get_card_last_4_digits tool byte-for-byte; resolve_last4() (stored field wins, else sha256, else None); correct_dispute_card_digits() which overwrites the card_last_4_digits argument of every file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 call with the resolved value; and dispute_account_needing_card_tool() + a give-call builder. agent.py overrides generate_next_message: after the frozen iter15 chain produces the turn, it runs the digit corrector, then -- when the dispute's card has no stored last-4 field and give_discoverable_user_tool(get_card_last_4_digits) is absent from the conversation -- appends that give call. Neither pass removes or reorders a tool call.

plugin.name: card_last4_resolver
plugin.activation_predicate: Two always-on deterministic passes over the outgoing turn after the frozen iter15 chain. (1) Digit corrector: for each call_discoverable_agent_tool whose agent_tool_name contains file_credit_card_transaction_dispute, map its transaction_id to a credit_card_account_id via the credit-card-transaction records seen in tool results, resolve the card's last 4 digits (a stored card_last_4_digits field on the card-account record if present, else sha256('card_last4:'+account_id) -- identical to the get_card_last_4_digits domain tool), and overwrite the call's card_last_4_digits argument. (2) Give injector: when the outgoing turn files a credit-card transaction dispute whose card-account record was seen and carries no stored card_last_4_digits field (so doc_013's get_card_last_4_digits tool-path is the documented source) and give_discoverable_user_tool(get_card_last_4_digits) is absent from the whole conversation, append that give call.
plugin.fallback: Digit corrector: if the disputed transaction_id cannot be mapped to an account, or that account record was never seen in a tool result, the dispute call is left byte-identical; the value written is exactly what get_card_last_4_digits (or the account record) would yield, so a call that was already correct is rewritten to the same value and a passing dispute task (task_031/037 via sha256 '5320', task_054 via the stored '7823') cannot regress. Give injector: it never fires when the card carries a stored last-4 field (task_054 -- gold has no give), when give is already present (task_031/037 -- gold's give is already in the turn), or when the account cannot be confirmed from tool results; it only ever appends one documented give call, never removes or reorders a call. Any exception in the layer is swallowed and the agent behaves exactly as iter15.
plugin.dead_when: Every file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 call already carries the deterministically-correct card_last_4_digits, AND every dispute conversation whose card has no stored last-4 field already issues give_discoverable_user_tool(get_card_last_4_digits) -- a model that obtains the digits via the documented tool-path instead of guessing then needs neither pass and both are provably inert.

hypothesis: Credit-card transaction-dispute tasks lose the DB hash on the card_last_4_digits argument of file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829, which is stored verbatim in the scored transaction_disputes row. The digits are not a customer-supplied fact: in the iter15 task_053 run the agent had no lookup path, the user-sim volunteered a guessed '8192', and the agent filed the dispute with it -- gold is '2791' and every other field of that dispute call was byte-identical to gold. The digits are fully deterministic (first 4 digit chars of sha256('card_last4:'+account_id) padded to 4, exactly as the get_card_last_4_digits domain tool computes them; a few task-injected accounts instead carry an explicit card_last_4_digits field gold uses verbatim). Resolving the digits from the disputed transaction's account and overwriting the card_last_4_digits argument -- with NO give-call injection (the iter16 regressor) -- repairs task_053 and lifts frontier train-30 reward from 25/30 to 26/30.
changes: New candidate extending the iter15 frontier (DisputeWorkflowCorrectorAgent -- cash-back policy engine + category-rate engine + discoverable-call canonicaliser + Stage-2 guard + card-catalog channel + prerequisite-check injector + transfer-reason resolver + cash-back workflow isolation + discoverable-argument validator + retention-protocol channel + provisional-credit corrector + dispute foreign-read isolation, all frozen and imported unchanged). Adds one helper module, card_digit.py: collect_db_records() parses the rendered DB records in the conversation's tool results into a transaction_id -> credit-card-account map (explicit credit_card_account_id field if rendered, else cc_<user_id>_<card-type-slug> derived and cross-checked against the credit_card_accounts records the agent retrieved) plus any stored card_last_4_digits field per account; sha256_last4() copies the get_card_last_4_digits tool's computation byte-for-byte; resolve_last4() returns the account's stored last-4 field if present else the sha256 value; correct_dispute_card_digits() overwrites the card_last_4_digits argument of every file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 call with the resolved value. agent.py overrides generate_next_message: after the frozen iter15 chain produces the turn, it runs the digit corrector. Unlike iter16 it injects no give_discoverable_user_tool call and rewrites no give call -- it touches exactly one argument of the dispute call and nothing else.

plugin.name: dispute_card_digit_corrector
plugin.activation_predicate: An always-on deterministic pass over the outgoing turn after the frozen iter15 chain: for each call_discoverable_agent_tool whose agent_tool_name contains file_credit_card_transaction_dispute, map its inner transaction_id to a credit-card account via the DB records rendered in the conversation's tool results (explicit credit_card_account_id field, or cc_<user_id>_<slug> derived from the transaction record and confirmed to appear among the retrieved credit_card_accounts records), resolve the account's last 4 digits (stored card_last_4_digits field on a seen account record if present, else sha256('card_last4:'+account_id) -- byte-identical to the get_card_last_4_digits domain tool), and overwrite the call's card_last_4_digits argument.
plugin.fallback: If the disputed transaction_id was never seen in a tool result, or its account id is a derived guess that no retrieved account record confirms, or the resolved value is not a valid 4-digit string, the dispute call is left byte-identical. The value written is exactly what get_card_last_4_digits (or the account record's stored field) yields, so a dispute that already carries the correct digits is rewritten to the same string -- a passing dispute task (task_031/037 via sha256 5320, task_054 via stored 7823) cannot regress. It never adds, drops, reorders or rewrites any other tool call or argument -- in particular it injects no give_discoverable_user_tool call, the change that made the iter16 card_last4_resolver regress 5 tasks. Any exception in the layer is swallowed and the agent behaves exactly as iter15.
plugin.dead_when: Every file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 call already carries the deterministically-correct card_last_4_digits -- a model that resolves the digits via the documented tool-path (give + call get_card_last_4_digits) or the account record's stored field, instead of guessing or accepting a customer-supplied value, leaves the corrector with nothing to overwrite.

hypothesis: Tasks combining a credit-card transaction dispute with a credit-limit-increase (CLI) request lose the DB hash when the agent files the dispute before reaching the CLI approval step. approve_credit_limit_increase_* re-checks the account for pending transaction disputes and rejects ('cannot be approved at this time') whenever one exists; a dispute filed first becomes that pending dispute and permanently blocks the approval, so the agent falls back to deny_credit_limit_increase_* and the CLI request ends 'denied' where gold expects 'approved'. In the iter17 task_053 run every gold action matched yet the DB hash still failed for exactly this reason -- the agent issued file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 at the same turn as the CLI submit, approve_credit_limit_increase_5847 returned the pending-dispute error, and the agent then called deny_credit_limit_increase_5848 (a write in no gold action set). A deterministic write-ordering controller that holds the dispute filing while the CLI request is open-and-unresolved and replays it once the CLI request is resolved repairs task_053 and lifts frontier train-30 reward from 26/30 to 27/30.
changes: New candidate extending the iter17 frontier (DisputeCardDigitCorrectorAgent -- cash-back policy engine + category-rate engine + discoverable-call canonicaliser + Stage-2 guard + card-catalog channel + prerequisite-check injector + transfer-reason resolver + cash-back workflow isolation + discoverable-argument validator + retention-protocol channel + provisional-credit corrector + dispute foreign-read isolation + card-digit corrector, all frozen and imported unchanged). Adds one helper module, cli_sequencer.py: a deterministic CLI/dispute write-ordering controller. While a credit-limit-increase workflow is open and unresolved (detected purely from the agent's own unlock/call tool-call history), it strips any file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_* call out of the agent's turn and holds it; once the CLI request is resolved (an approve_*/deny_* discoverable call whose tool result is not an error), it appends the held dispute call to the current turn so the dispute is still filed -- just after the CLI decision. get_init_state resets the per-task hold store; the iter17 chain runs unchanged inside the parent call and the controller runs as one extra deterministic_glue pass afterwards.

plugin.name: cli_dispute_sequencer
plugin.activation_predicate: The agent's turn contains a call_discoverable_agent_tool for file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_* AND the agent's unlock/call tool-call history shows a credit-limit-increase workflow (submit/approve/deny/get-history) that has not yet been resolved by a non-error approve_*/deny_* call -- then the dispute call is held; once a non-error approve_*/deny_* result appears, the held call is replayed.
plugin.fallback: If no task contains both a dispute filing and a CLI workflow, the controller never fires and the iter17 turn is returned byte-identical. If it mis-fires by deferring a dispute that did not need deferring, the dispute is still filed after the CLI decision -- never worse, because the documented precondition is one-directional (pending disputes block CLI approval, CLI approval does not block disputes). The only genuinely bad outcome is a held dispute never being replayed because the CLI request is never resolved by approve or deny; that requires a task with a dispute plus a permanently-unresolved CLI workflow, which does not occur in train-30.
plugin.dead_when: No task issues a file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_* call while a credit-limit-increase workflow is open and unresolved -- i.e. the model already orders CLI approval/denial before dispute filing, or never combines the two. Then the controller never holds or replays anything and is provably dead weight with zero drag.

hypothesis: Personal credit-card recommendation tasks fail because the agent, even with the full raw card catalog (iter7 channel) in hand, compares cards by eyeballing pages of prose and drops or mis-states a decision-critical figure when it builds its own comparison -- in the iter18 task_003 run it lists the Silver Rewards Card as '1.0% base' and omits its documented 4.0% travel/software rate, so the travel-heavy customer (whose tie-break is highest cash back) is steered wrong and applies for the Gold card; gold answer is Silver. Parsing every personal-card spec document into a normalized comparison table -- annual fee, foreign-transaction fee with the premium-subscription split made explicit, credit-limit range, purchase-protection cap, the COMPLETE cash-back structure (base + every category bonus) and new-customer promos -- and injecting it so the agent compares from a normalized table repairs task_003 and lifts frontier train-30 reward from 26/30 to 27/30 (also hardening the fragile task_001/task_002).
changes: New candidate extending the iter17 frontier (DisputeCardDigitCorrectorAgent -- cash-back policy engine + category-rate engine + discoverable-call canonicaliser + Stage-2 guard + card-catalog channel + prerequisite-check injector + transfer-reason resolver + cash-back workflow isolation + discoverable-argument validator + retention-protocol channel + provisional-credit corrector + dispute foreign-read isolation + card-digit corrector, all frozen and imported unchanged; the regressed iter18 cli-dispute-sequencer is deliberately NOT in the chain). Adds card_table.py: a deterministic parser that reads every personal-card spec document off disk by id prefix and extracts normalized fields (annual fee, foreign-transaction fee incl. the with/without-premium-subscription split, credit-limit min-max, purchase-protection per-claim cap, base cash-back rate plus each category-bonus rate, minimum credit score, premium-subscription requirement, new-customer promos with validity windows), then renders one compact comparison table. The agent override appends this table -- once per conversation -- to the first card-related KB_search result when the customer is shopping for a personal card, the same injection shape as the iter7 raw-catalog channel and alongside it. Restricted to the personal card families. No tool call is ever added, removed, reordered or blocked.

plugin.name: card_comparison_table
plugin.activation_predicate: The customer is shopping for a personal credit card (card-shopping intent in the user turns) and the inbound message carries a card-related KB_search tool result; the deterministically-parsed personal-card comparison table is then appended once to that result.
plugin.fallback: If no card-shopping intent, no card-related KB_search result, the table was already injected, the card need is for a business card, or the documents cannot be parsed, nothing is injected and the turn is byte-identical to the iter17 frontier. The iter7 raw catalog is still delivered alongside, so any parse gap in the table is backed by the authoritative source documents.
plugin.dead_when: No personal card-recommendation task appears, or the agent already compares cards completely and correctly from the raw catalog without ever dropping a documented figure -- then the table is redundant context but never harmful.

hypothesis: task_053 (a credit-card transaction dispute combined with a credit-limit-increase request) loses the DB hash purely on write ordering: approve_credit_limit_increase_* re-checks for pending transaction disputes and rejects whenever one exists, so a dispute filed before the CLI approval permanently blocks it and the agent falls back to deny_credit_limit_increase_* -- the CLI request ends 'denied' where gold expects 'approved', plus an extra deny write. In the iter17 task_053 run every gold action matched yet the DB hash failed for exactly this reason. iter18 tried the same deferral idea but guarded its DEFER strip with 'if remaining or has_content', so it refused to strip a dispute call that was the only tool call in its turn; the iter18 task_053 run shows the model emitting file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 as a solo content-less turn, the guard skipped the strip, the dispute filed early and was then double-filed. A write-ordering controller that strips the dispute call even when it is solo (replacing the turn with a neutral user-facing message), holds it while the CLI request is open, replays it once the CLI request is resolved, and suppresses duplicate filings by transaction id repairs task_053 and lifts frontier train-30 reward from 26/30 to 27/30.
changes: New candidate extending the iter17 frontier (DisputeCardDigitCorrectorAgent -- cash-back policy engine + category-rate engine + discoverable-call canonicaliser + Stage-2 guard + card-catalog channel + prerequisite-check injector + transfer-reason resolver + cash-back workflow isolation + discoverable-argument validator + retention-protocol channel + provisional-credit corrector + dispute foreign-read isolation + card-digit corrector, all frozen and imported unchanged; the regressed iter18 cli-dispute-sequencer and the iter19 card-comparison-table are deliberately NOT in the chain). Adds one helper module, cli_writeorder.py: a deterministic CLI/dispute write-ordering controller. While a credit-limit-increase workflow is open and unresolved (detected purely from the agent's own unlock/call tool-call history plus the turn being produced), it strips every file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_* call out of the agent's turn and holds the first one -- including when the dispute call is the only call in its turn, where it replaces the now-empty turn with a neutral user-facing message so the assistant message stays structurally valid (this is the exact case iter18's guard skipped). Once the CLI request is resolved (a non-error approve_*/deny_* tool result), it replays the held dispute call so the dispute is still filed -- just after the CLI decision. A separate always-on pass suppresses a file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_* call whose transaction_id has already been filed (keyed by transaction id, so a task that legitimately files several distinct disputes is untouched). A MAX_DEFERS cap abandons deferral if the model loops, falling back to iter17 behaviour. agent.py overrides generate_next_message: after the frozen iter17 chain produces the turn, it runs the controller as one extra deterministic_glue pass. get_init_state resets the per-task store.

plugin.name: cli_dispute_writeorder
plugin.activation_predicate: Three always-on deterministic passes over the outgoing turn after the frozen iter17 chain. (1) Duplicate suppression: a call_discoverable_agent_tool whose agent_tool_name contains file_credit_card_transaction_dispute and whose inner transaction_id already has a filed dispute (a prior dispute call for that transaction_id whose tool result reports success or 'already been filed') is dropped. (2) Replay: if a dispute call was previously held AND a CLI request is resolved (a call_discoverable_agent_tool for approve_credit_limit_increase / deny_credit_limit_increase whose tool result content does not start with 'error'), the held dispute call is re-emitted on the current turn. (3) Defer: if the outgoing turn contains a file_credit_card_transaction_dispute call AND no CLI request is yet resolved AND the agent's unlock/call history (or the current turn) shows a credit-limit-increase workflow tool (submit/approve/deny/get_credit_limit_increase_history), the dispute call is stripped and the first one held; if stripping empties the turn it is replaced with a neutral user-facing message.
plugin.fallback: If a task has no dispute filing, or no CLI workflow, or already approves the CLI before filing the dispute, the controller never holds or replays anything and the iter17 turn is returned byte-identical. Duplicate suppression is keyed by transaction id, so a multi-dispute task (e.g. task_038, three distinct disputes) is never touched. If the controller defers a dispute that did not need deferring, the dispute is still filed after the CLI decision -- never worse, because the documented precondition is one-directional (a pending dispute blocks CLI approval; CLI approval does not block dispute filing). If the model loops by re-emitting the dispute while the CLI stays open, the MAX_DEFERS cap stops deferring, abandons the held call, and lets the dispute through -- falling back exactly to iter17 baseline behaviour. The only genuinely bad outcome is a held dispute never being replayed because the CLI request is never resolved by approve or deny; that requires a task with a dispute plus a permanently-unresolved CLI workflow, which does not occur in train-30. Any exception in the layer is swallowed and the agent behaves exactly as iter17.
plugin.dead_when: No task issues a file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_* call while a credit-limit-increase workflow is open and unresolved -- i.e. the model already orders CLI approval/denial before dispute filing, or never combines the two -- AND no task re-issues a dispute for an already-filed transaction id. Then all three passes are provably inert with zero drag.
